Mirror coating work orders

An observatory needs a Normalizer ledger for mirror coatings. Orders arrive together by mirror_serial, in event order; mirror serials are nonnegative. A different serial represents an independent coating account. KEEP commissions a prescription and REMOVE withdraws it. A withdrawal does not read reflectance_card. A later commissioning after withdrawal is a new installation.

Check workday_spelling as a complete yyyy-MM-dd calendar date, without surrounding spaces, interpreted as midnight UTC. KEEP also needs reflectance_card, trimmed, with an optional minus sign, one to six ASCII integer digits and an optional decimal point followed by one or two digits. Any failed check or unknown work_order produces INVALID, defect_note INPUT, and leaves the usable coating account untouched.

For a usable KEEP, compare the exact reflectance with the preceding usable KEEP for this serial, including one that produced UNCHANGED. Compare coating_alloy with the installed alloy after trimming and uppercasing; absent alloy agrees with blank. A difference in either comparison replaces the coating. Keep raw alloy spelling in the ledger. Replacement writes CLOSE before OPEN; the former describes the installed coating, never the equivalent intervening proposal. A commissioning with no coating in service writes OPEN. An equivalent order writes UNCHANGED. REMOVE writes CLOSE then RETIRED when in service, otherwise INACTIVE.

OPEN gets one long coating_keys number, starting 8001 with increment 1, as coating_revision; it stores exact reflectance_pct and coating_start. CLOSE reuses that revision and payload with coating_end equal to the withdrawal/replacement day; OPEN ends at null. Other events have null revision, reflectance, alloy and endpoints. Every row copies mirror_serial and docket_ref, sets ledger_event, and supplies accounting_month as UTC yyyy-MM, for example 2026-01, or empty if its day is invalid. defect_note is empty except on INVALID. Port 0 retains event order. inspection_ts, spare_budget, courier_note and line_no have no decision role.

Fountain commissioning register

Build a Normalizer for the parks fountain commissioning register. Each consecutive fountain_no block is a separate installation account, with no imported target rows. Fountain numbers are nonnegative. Source order within a block is authoritative.

The commissioning pressure is anchored to the first usable KEEP following the start of that account or a REMOVE. Even if later work replaces the nozzle, that commissioning pressure remains the numerical reference until withdrawal. A pressure difference of at least 2.00 bar from it warrants replacement. nozzle_stamp can also warrant replacement: compare its trimmed spelling, preserving letter case, with absent and blank equivalent. Installed rows retain the submitted stamp untrimmed. Equivalent orders are silent.

KEEP reads trimmed pressure_entry: allow a minus sign, one through six ASCII digits, and optionally a dot with one or two further digits. Both directives require activation_day spelled exactly yyyy-MM-dd and valid in the UTC calendar. REMOVE ignores pressure_entry. An unknown directive, malformed pressure on KEEP, or invalid date yields INVALID with rejection_code INPUT; such paperwork does not alter the usable installation account.

Port 0 carries register_kind OPEN for installation, CLOSE followed by OPEN for replacement, CLOSE alone for active withdrawal, and INACTIVE for a withdrawal with nothing installed. Recommissioning after withdrawal creates OPEN. Long sequence nozzle_keys starts at 8001, increment 1; only OPEN receives a fresh nozzle_revision. For OPEN record pressure_bar, raw nozzle_stamp and live_since, leaving live_until null. A CLOSE must reproduce the old revision, pressure, stamp and starting date, ending at the current activation day. INVALID and INACTIVE contain null installation payload. Copy fountain_no and permit_scan onto each event. permit_month is the valid UTC day formatted yyyy-MM, such as 2026-02, otherwise empty; rejection_code is otherwise empty. estimate_cost, crew_arrival, service_comment and visit_order are unused.

Heliostat focus classes

The solar field needs a Normalizer that records changes of optical class rather than every measurement. Receive each heliostat_number as one consecutive block of ordered events; heliostat numbers are nonnegative. KEEP proposes focal distance and surface finish, while REMOVE withdraws the prescription. Reinstallation is allowed.

A numerical class is the focal distance rounded to a whole decimal with halves away from zero. Compare a usable KEEP with the preceding usable KEEP, even when that earlier measurement needed no installation. Different classes trigger replacement. Independently, compare surface_finish exactly as nullable raw text: null differs from empty and spaces matter. Replacement is needed if either comparison differs. An equivalent KEEP becomes UNCHANGED without modifying the installed payload.

The event day effective_sheet_day must match ten-character yyyy-MM-dd and a possible UTC calendar date. Trim focal_distance_note for KEEP, allowing an optional minus, one to six ASCII integer digits and an optional dot with one or two fraction digits. REMOVE disregards distance text. Any invalid requirement or unrecognised movement yields INVALID and paperwork_code INPUT, retaining the existing usable optical account.

Send OPEN for a first installation, CLOSE then OPEN for replacement, CLOSE then RETIRED for withdrawal in service, and INACTIVE for withdrawal otherwise. Every emitted row copies heliostat_number and field_ticket, fills focus_event, and gives solar_month as the event's UTC yyyy-MM month, e.g. 2026-03, or empty for an invalid date. Other paperwork_code values are empty. Sequence optics_keys supplies long optical_revision values from 8001 by 1 only when OPEN is emitted. OPEN stores unrounded focal_distance, raw surface_finish and installed_on with removed_on null. CLOSE preserves the installed revision, distance, finish and installed_on, ending on this event's day. Audit events have all five installation fields null. reserve_cost, measurement_time, technician_message and row_number are irrelevant to these decisions.

Reef circulation prescriptions

A reef laboratory distinguishes reverse circulation from forward circulation in nursery_bay accounts. Each bay's requests are consecutive; bay numbers are nonnegative. Implement the prescription feed as a Normalizer, retaining source event order on its only output.

For this laboratory, negative circulation is one class and nonnegative circulation another. The class of the first successful KEEP of an installation cycle governs subsequent comparisons until REMOVE, even if replacement pumps were installed in between. mesh_grade is an additional independent replacement criterion; trim it and ignore case, with null equivalent to whitespace. Preserve its original spelling in installed records. Comparing within the same class and grade creates UNCHANGED. A changed class or grade creates CLOSE followed by OPEN.

request_type KEEP requires a circulation_reading that, after trim, has optional minus, one to six ASCII integer digits and at most two fractional digits after an optional dot. REMOVE ignores the reading. service_day is mandatory for either request and must be exactly yyyy-MM-dd with a real UTC calendar day. Unknown requests and defective paperwork produce one INVALID, repair_code INPUT. They cannot change which pump prescription is usable.

An installation with nothing currently enabled emits OPEN. REMOVE emits CLOSE only when enabled and otherwise emits nothing; a later KEEP starts a new installation cycle. OPEN alone draws a long pump_keys value (8001, increment 1) into pump_revision. Its circulation_rate, raw mesh_grade and enabled_day describe the proposal; disabled_day is null. A CLOSE retains the installed revision, rate, mesh and enabled_day, ending at service_day. Audit payload fields are null. Set circulation_event and copy nursery_bay and dive_record to every row. restoration_month contains the valid event month in UTC yyyy-MM form, for example 2026-01, or empty when invalid. repair_code is empty for all other events. grant_amount, diver_checkin, reef_comment and sampling_order have no operational effect.

Glacier mount inclination records

For a glacier expedition, write a Normalizer that turns ordered mounting operations into an installation ledger. sensor_mount blocks are consecutive, and mount numbers are nonnegative. KEEP proposes an inclination and bracket; REMOVE takes a mount out of service.

The relevant inclination categories are exactly zero and everything nonzero. Each usable KEEP is compared with the preceding usable KEEP for this mount. bracket_mark is compared with the bracket on the installed prescription; null and empty are equivalent, while whitespace and case are significant. A category or bracket difference requires CLOSE then OPEN. An equivalent submission gives UNCHANGED, without rewriting the installed angle or bracket. Usable equivalent inclinations still participate in the next numerical comparison.

installation_day denotes midnight UTC and must use the complete yyyy-MM-dd spelling of a possible calendar day. KEEP's inclination_entry is trimmed and must contain optional minus, one to six ASCII integer digits and optionally a dot plus one or two digits. REMOVE needs no inclination. Unknown operation, malformed required inclination or invalid day writes INVALID with damage_code INPUT; usable installations are unaffected by this paperwork.

The first KEEP while out of service gives OPEN. Active REMOVE gives CLOSE then RETIRED, and an inactive REMOVE gives INACTIVE. Reinstallation starts with another OPEN. Allocate one long mounting_revision from mount_keys, beginning 8001 with step 1, for OPEN only. OPEN stores exact inclination_degrees, raw bracket_mark and fitted_day, leaving unfitted_day null. CLOSE carries that installed revision, angle, bracket and fitted_day, with unfitted_day the day before installation_day in the UTC calendar. Audits have null installation fields. Every row sets mount_event, copies sensor_mount and expedition_page, and formats expedition_month as yyyy-MM from a valid UTC event day, e.g. 2026-01; otherwise it is empty. damage_code is empty except for INVALID. Ignore freight_estimate, radio_received, field_annotation and arrival_no.

Farm rack lighting bands

A vertical farm commissions lighting schedules by growing_rack. Feed consecutive rack blocks into a Normalizer; rack numbers are nonnegative. The first usable KEEP after a block begins or after REMOVE sets the commissioning band for that installation cycle.

Lighting bands are mathematical floor(lamp hours divided by 3), including negative quantities. Replacement decisions continue to use the commissioning band even after a replacement OPEN. spectral_recipe also matters: compare nullable text exactly, including case and spaces; absent differs from empty. A band or recipe difference produces CLOSE then OPEN. A matching proposal produces UNCHANGED. Repeated agreement does not rewrite the installed schedule's payload.

The work sheet adjustment is KEEP or REMOVE. KEEP reads trimmed lamp_hours_slip with an optional minus sign, one through six ASCII integer digits and optionally a decimal point with one or two fractional digits. REMOVE disregards the slip. Both require sowing_day to name an actual UTC calendar day, with exact yyyy-MM-dd spelling. Any unknown adjustment or failed input requirement produces INVALID, input_fault INPUT, without modifying the usable lighting account.

OPEN is also emitted when KEEP finds no schedule operating. REMOVE closes an operating schedule and is silent otherwise. Another KEEP following withdrawal commissions a new cycle. Only OPEN takes one long value from lighting_keys, start 8001, step 1, as recipe_revision. It records the unrounded lamp_hours, raw spectral_recipe and schedule_start with schedule_finish null. CLOSE reproduces the installed revision, hours, recipe and start, and sets schedule_finish to this event's sowing_day. Audit installation fields are null. Copy growing_rack and crop_sheet to each row; fill lighting_notice and harvest_month, the event UTC month formatted yyyy-MM, e.g. 2026-06, empty for an invalid day. input_fault is otherwise empty. seed_cost, controller_time, agronomist_note and reading_order are unused.

Acoustic baffle absorption changes

The acoustics laboratory needs a Normalizer for baffle prescriptions, with events adjacent by chamber_baffle and in test order. Baffle numbers are nonnegative. There are no imported versions.

A usable KEEP is numerically significant only when its absorption is lower than the preceding usable KEEP for that baffle. Even a higher or equal usable observation becomes the next comparison point. The installed cloth remains the descriptor reference: trim cloth_description, retaining case, and consider absent equivalent to blank. A different cloth also triggers replacement, regardless of absorption direction. If neither comparison triggers, emit UNCHANGED while retaining the last installed payload.

KEEP installs an out-of-service baffle with OPEN, or replaces an operating one with CLOSE then OPEN. REMOVE writes CLOSE then RETIRED if operating and INACTIVE otherwise. KEEP after withdrawal may install anew. Any unknown instruction_code is INVALID. For both known instructions test_day must be exactly yyyy-MM-dd and a real UTC day. Only KEEP requires absorption_note; trim it and accept optional minus, one to six ASCII digits and an optional dot with one or two digits. Invalid paperwork writes one INVALID, worksheet_error INPUT, and cannot affect usable baffle decisions.

OPEN gets one long baffle_keys number, beginning at 8001 and advancing by 1. Store it in baffle_revision with exact absorption_ratio, raw cloth_description and usable_from, leaving usable_to null. CLOSE uses the old installed revision, absorption, cloth and starting date; its usable_to is this event day. UNCHANGED, RETIRED, INACTIVE and INVALID have null installation payload. Copy chamber_baffle and trial_sheet to all rows, identify baffle_notice, and fill testing_month with the UTC yyyy-MM month, e.g. 2026-05, empty when the day fails validation. worksheet_error is otherwise empty. fabric_cost, laboratory_time, test_comment and observation_no are unrelated provenance.

Seed vault ventilation tolerances

Seed-bank engineers need a Normalizer ledger for ventilation prescriptions. Receive ordered vault_duct blocks, each describing one independent duct; duct numbers are nonnegative. There is no target-side opening balance.

For each installation cycle, its commissioning KEEP supplies the airflow reference until REMOVE. A later replacement does not move that reference. Replace when the absolute proposed airflow difference exceeds 1.00; equality at that boundary is equivalent. A filter_grade difference also replaces: absence and empty agree, but other raw characters must match exactly. Save raw filter spelling. An equivalent proposal emits UNCHANGED and leaves the installation payload as commissioned or last replaced.

order_type has KEEP and REMOVE meanings. KEEP installs an idle duct with OPEN. A replacement is CLOSE then OPEN. REMOVE emits CLOSE for an operating duct or INACTIVE for an idle one; reinstallation is permitted. Validate storage_day for either operation as an exact ten-character yyyy-MM-dd UTC calendar date. A KEEP additionally needs trimmed airflow_form consisting of optional minus, one to six ASCII integer digits and an optional dot followed by one or two digits. REMOVE ignores airflow_form. Unknown operations and defective required fields yield INVALID, form_defect INPUT, without disturbing usable prescriptions.

Only OPEN consumes a long ventilation_keys identifier, from 8001 by 1, recorded as duct_revision. Its airflow_setting, raw filter_grade and effective_from describe the proposal, and effective_to is null. CLOSE preserves the installed revision, airflow, filter and starting date; effective_to is the preceding UTC calendar day relative to storage_day. Other events have null installation payload. All output copies vault_duct and maintenance_scan and fills ventilation_event. preservation_month is yyyy-MM from the valid UTC event day, such as 2026-01, or empty if invalid; form_defect is otherwise empty. service_allowance, receipt_clock, operator_comment and worksheet_no are unused.
